questions.text: निम्नलिखित अभिक्रियाओं में से किसका स्पष्टीकरण ग्लूकोस की विवृत श्रृंखला संरचना द्वारा नहीं किया जाता है ?
questions.text_english: Which of the following reactions is not explained by the open chain structure of glucose ?

options.A: HI के साथ लंबे समय तक गरम करने पर ग्लूकोस n-हेक्सेन देता है।
options.B: ग्लूकोस, हाइड्रॉक्सिल ऐमीन के साथ अभिक्रिया करके एक ऑक्सिम देता है।
options.C: ब्रोमीन जल के साथ अभिक्रिया करके ग्लूकोस ऑक्सीकृत होकर ग्लूकोनिक अम्ल देता है।
options.D: ग्लूकोस दो भिन्न क्रिस्टलीय रूपों, अल्फा (α) और बीटा (β) में पाया जाता है।

options_english.A: Glucose on prolonged heating with HI forms n-hexane.
options_english.B: Glucose reacts with hydroxylamine to form an oxime.
options_english.C: Glucose gets oxidized to gluconic acid on reaction with bromine water.
options_english.D: Glucose exists in two different crystalline forms, alpha (α) and beta (β).

questions.solution: Option D is correct. The existence of glucose in two crystalline forms, alpha and beta (anomers), is explained by the cyclic (ring) structure of glucose, not the open chain structure. The open chain structure explains reactions with HI (reduction to n-hexane), with hydroxylamine (oxime formation), and with bromine water (oxidation to gluconic acid) because these reactions involve the aldehyde group present in the open chain form. Anomer formation arises due to the cyclization of glucose and the creation of a new chiral centre at C-1, which cannot be explained by the open chain structure.
questions.solution_hindi: विकल्प D सही है। ग्लूकोस का दो क्रिस्टलीय रूपों (अल्फा और बीटा) में पाया जाना चक्रीय संरचना द्वारा समझाया जाता है, विवृत श्रृंखला संरचना द्वारा नहीं।

questions.text: प्रोटीन α-ऐमीनो अम्लों के बहुलक होते हैं जो आपस में जुड़े होते हैं
questions.text_english: Proteins are polymers of α-amino acids which are joined to each other by :
questions.solution: Option B is correct. Proteins are formed by the condensation of α-amino acids through peptide bonds. A peptide bond is formed between the amino group (–NH2) of one amino acid and the carboxyl group (–COOH) of another amino acid with the elimination of a water molecule. Glycosidic bonds link monosaccharides in carbohydrates, not amino acids. Covalent and coordinate bonds are too broad and not specific to amino acid linkage in proteins.
questions.solution_hindi: विकल्प B सही है। प्रोटीन में α-ऐमीनो अम्ल पेप्टाइड आबंध द्वारा जुड़े होते हैं।

questions.text: क्षारक जो DNA में उपस्थित है, लेकिन RNA में नहीं है
questions.text_english: The base which is present in DNA but not in RNA is :
questions.solution: Option C is correct. Thymine (5-methyluracil) is a pyrimidine base found exclusively in DNA. In RNA, thymine is replaced by Uracil. Both Guanine and Cytosine are present in DNA as well as RNA (as complementary base pairs). Adenine is also present in both DNA and RNA. Therefore, thymine is the base present in DNA but absent in RNA.
questions.solution_hindi: विकल्प C सही है। थायमीन केवल DNA में पाया जाता है, RNA में नहीं। RNA में थायमीन के स्थान पर यूरेसिल होता है।

questions.text: लीथियम एल्युमिनियम हाइड्राइड के साथ एथेननाइट्राइल के अपचयन द्वारा उत्पादित यौगिक को पहचानिए :
questions.text_english: Identify the compound produced by the reduction of Ethanenitrile with Lithium aluminium hydride :
questions.solution: Option A is correct. Ethanenitrile (CH3CN) has 2 carbon atoms. When reduced with LiAlH4, the nitrile group (–C≡N) is reduced to an amine group (–CH2NH2). The product is ethylamine (CH3CH2NH2), which also has 2 carbon atoms. Propylamine would require 3 carbons, and methylamine only 1. Ethanal is an aldehyde produced by a different type of reduction (partial reduction of acid chloride), not from a nitrile.
questions.solution_hindi: विकल्प A सही है। एथेननाइट्राइल (CH3CN) का LiAlH4 से अपचयन करने पर एथिलऐमीन (CH3CH2NH2) प्राप्त होती है।

questions.text: दिए हुए यौगिकों के क्वथनांकों के सही बढ़ते क्रम को पहचानिए :
questions.text_english: Identify the correct increasing order of boiling points of the given compounds :
questions.solution: Option C is correct. Boiling points of alcohols increase with increasing molecular mass (more carbons = higher bp). Among structural isomers (same molecular formula), branching decreases the surface area and thus lowers the boiling point. Propan-1-ol (3C, bp 97°C) < Butan-2-ol (4C, branched, bp 99.5°C) < Butan-1-ol (4C, straight chain, bp 117°C) < Pentan-1-ol (5C, bp 138°C). This matches option C.
questions.solution_hindi: विकल्प C सही है। क्वथनांक का सही बढ़ता क्रम: प्रोपेन-1-ऑल < ब्यूटेन-2-ऑल < ब्यूटेन-1-ऑल < पेन्टेन-1-ऑल।

questions.text: निम्नलिखित अणुओं में से किसकी प्रकृति काइरल है ?
questions.text_english: Which of the following molecules is chiral in nature ?
questions.solution: Option B is correct. A chiral molecule has a carbon atom bearing four different substituents (a chiral/asymmetric centre). Butan-2-ol (CH3CHOHCH2CH3) has C-2 bearing –OH, –H, –CH3, and –CH2CH3, which are all four different groups, making it chiral. Propan-2-ol has C-2 bearing –OH, –H, –CH3, and –CH3; the two methyl groups are identical, so it is achiral. 1-Bromobutane has no asymmetric carbon. 2-Bromopropane has C-2 bearing –Br, –H, –CH3, and –CH3; the two methyls are identical, so it is achiral.
questions.solution_hindi: विकल्प B सही है। ब्यूटेन-2-ऑल में C-2 पर चार भिन्न समूह हैं, अतः यह काइरल है।

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से कौन हेटरोलेप्टिक संकुल है ?
questions.text_english: Which of the following is heteroleptic complex ?
questions.solution: Option D is correct. A heteroleptic complex contains two or more different types of ligands coordinated to the central metal atom. [Co(NH3)4Cl2]+ contains both NH3 and Cl– as ligands (two different types), making it heteroleptic. The other three complexes — [Co(NH3)6]3+, [Cr(NH3)6]3+, and [Ni(H2O)6]2+ — each contain only one type of ligand (homoleptic complexes).
questions.solution_hindi: विकल्प D सही है। [Co(NH3)4Cl2]+ में दो भिन्न प्रकार के लिगैंड (NH3 और Cl–) हैं, अतः यह हेटरोलेप्टिक है।

questions.text: संकुल [Pt(NH3)2Cl2] का सही IUPAC नाम है
questions.text_english: The correct IUPAC name of the complex [Pt(NH3)2Cl2] is :
questions.solution: Option B is correct. In IUPAC nomenclature of coordination compounds, ligands are named in alphabetical order before the metal. NH3 ligand is named 'ammine' and Cl– ligand is named 'chlorido'. Since there are two each, prefixes 'di' are added. The name becomes diamminedichlorido. Platinum here has oxidation state: let it be x; x + 0 + 0 + 2(–1) = 0, so x = +2, giving platinum(II). Ligands are named alphabetically: 'a' (ammine) before 'c' (chlorido), so diamminedichloridoplatinum(II) is correct.
questions.solution_hindi: विकल्प B सही है। Pt की ऑक्सीकरण अवस्था +2 है। IUPAC नाम: डाइऐम्मीनडाइक्लोरिडोप्लैटिनम (II)।

questions.text: क्रोमियम का इलेक्ट्रॉनिक विन्यास है
questions.text_english: Electronic configuration of chromium is :
questions.solution: Option C is correct. Chromium (Cr, Z = 24) has the electronic configuration [Ar] 3d5 4s1, not the expected [Ar] 3d4 4s2. This anomalous configuration arises because a half-filled d subshell (3d5) gives extra stability due to exchange energy. One electron from the 4s orbital shifts to the 3d orbital to achieve this stable half-filled configuration. Option D ([Ar] 3d5 4s2) would be the expected but incorrect configuration.
questions.solution_hindi: विकल्प C सही है। क्रोमियम का इलेक्ट्रॉनिक विन्यास [Ar] 3d5 4s1 है क्योंकि अर्धपूर्ण d कक्षक अतिरिक्त स्थायित्व देता है।

questions.text:
दी हुई अभिक्रिया की कोटि है
A + 2B → उत्पादों
वेग = k[A]½ [B]1
questions.text_english:
The order for the given reaction is :
A + 2B → Products
Rate = k[A]½ [B]1
questions.solution: Option A is correct. The overall order of a reaction is the sum of the powers of concentration terms in the rate law. Here, Rate = k[A]½[B]1. Order with respect to A = ½ = 0.5, and order with respect to B = 1. Therefore, overall order = 0.5 + 1 = 1.5. Note that the stoichiometric coefficients in the balanced equation do not determine the order; only the experimentally determined exponents in the rate law do.
questions.solution_hindi: विकल्प A सही है। कुल कोटि = ½ + 1 = 1.5।

questions.text_english: Identify the correct statement :

options.A: अभिक्रिया की आण्विकता एक प्रायोगिक मात्रा है।
options.B: जटिल अभिक्रियाओं के लिए आण्विकता का कोई अर्थ नहीं होता।
options.C: अभिक्रिया की आण्विकता शून्य अथवा भिन्नात्मक भी हो सकती है।
options.D: रासायनिक अभिक्रियाओं में तीन से अधिक आण्विकता अत्यधिक आम है।

options_english.A: Molecularity of a reaction is an experimental quantity.
options_english.B: For complex reactions molecularity has no meaning.
options_english.C: Molecularity of a reaction can be zero or even a fraction.
options_english.D: Molecularity more than three is very common in chemical reactions.

questions.solution: Option B is correct. Molecularity is defined only for elementary (simple) reactions and refers to the number of molecules colliding simultaneously in a single step. For complex (multi-step) reactions, only individual elementary steps have a molecularity; the overall reaction does not. Molecularity is always a whole number (1, 2, or rarely 3) and is a theoretical concept, not an experimental quantity (that makes option A wrong). It can never be zero or a fraction (option C wrong). Molecularity greater than three is extremely rare, not common (option D wrong).
questions.solution_hindi: विकल्प B सही है। जटिल अभिक्रियाओं के लिए आण्विकता का अर्थ नहीं होता; यह केवल प्राथमिक अभिक्रिया के प्रत्येक चरण पर लागू होती है।

questions.text:
निम्नलिखित अभिक्रिया पर विचार कीजिए :
Zn(s) + Ag2O(s) + H2O(l) → Zn2+(aq) + 2Ag(s) + 2OH–(aq)
दिया है: E°Ag+/Ag = 0.80 V, E°Zn2+/Zn = –0.76 V, 1 F = 96500 C mol–1
उपरोक्त अभिक्रिया की ΔrG° है :
questions.text_english:
Consider the following reaction :
Zn(s) + Ag2O(s) + H2O(l) → Zn2+(aq) + 2Ag(s) + 2OH–(aq)
Given : E°Ag+/Ag = 0.80 V, E°Zn2+/Zn = –0.76 V, 1 F = 96500 C mol–1
ΔrG° for the above reaction is :
questions.solution: Option A is correct. E°cell = E°cathode – E°anode = E°Ag+/Ag – E°Zn2+/Zn = 0.80 – (–0.76) = 1.56 V. The number of electrons transferred n = 2 (Zn → Zn2+ + 2e–). ΔrG° = –nFE°cell = –2 × 96500 × 1.56 = –301080 J mol–1 = –301.080 kJ mol–1. This matches option A.

अभिकथन (A) : ग्लूकोस, ब्रोमीन जल द्वारा ऑक्सीकृत होकर छः कार्बन परमाणुयुक्त ग्लूकोनिक अम्ल बनाता है।
कारण (R) : ग्लूकोस की विवृत श्रृंखला संरचना में कार्बोनिल समूह अनुपस्थित है।

Assertion (A) : Glucose gets oxidized to six carbon gluconic acid on reaction with bromine water.
Reason (R) : The carbonyl group is absent in the open chain structure of glucose.
questions.instruction_line: निम्नलिखित में से सही उत्तर चुनिए:
questions.instruction_line_english: Select the correct answer from the codes given below:

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सही है, परन्तु कारण (R) गलत है।

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

questions.solution: Option C is correct. Assertion A is true: glucose is indeed oxidized by bromine water to gluconic acid (a six-carbon acid), which confirms the presence of an aldehyde group in glucose. However, Reason R is false: the open chain structure of glucose does contain a carbonyl group (–CHO, aldehyde group) at C-1. It is precisely because of this aldehyde group that glucose is oxidized by bromine water. If the carbonyl group were absent, glucose would not react with bromine water.
questions.solution_hindi: विकल्प C सही है। अभिकथन सही है परन्तु कारण गलत है। ग्लूकोस की विवृत श्रृंखला में –CHO (कार्बोनिल) समूह उपस्थित होता है।

Reason (R) : Aryl halides do not undergo nucleophilic substitution with the anion formed by phthalimide.

options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है।

options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

questions.solution: Option D is correct. Assertion A is false: Gabriel phthalimide synthesis cannot be used to prepare aromatic primary amines because the method requires an alkyl halide, and aryl halides do not undergo the required nucleophilic substitution. Reason R is true: aryl halides do not undergo nucleophilic substitution reactions readily due to the partial double bond character between the carbon and halogen in aryl halides (resonance stabilization), so the phthalimide anion cannot attack them. Since Assertion is false but Reason is true, option D is correct.
questions.solution_hindi: विकल्प D सही है। अभिकथन गलत है (ऐरोमैटिक प्राथमिक ऐमीन गैब्रिएल संश्लेषण से नहीं बन सकती), परन्तु कारण सही है।

Transition elements are defined as those whose atoms or ions have incompletely filled d orbitals. Zn (3d10 4s2), Cd (4d10 5s2), and Hg (5d10 6s2) all have completely filled d orbitals in both their ground state and in their common oxidation state (+2), i.e., Zn2+ is 3d10. questions.solution: Option A is correct. Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason correctly explains Assertion. The decomposition of HI (2HI → H2 + I2) is a bimolecular elementary reaction. Molecularity refers to the number of reactant molecules (or species) that simultaneously collide and react in a single elementary step. Since two HI molecules collide simultaneously to give products, the molecularity is 2. The Reason correctly explains this.

sub_questions.text_english: Why is third ionization enthalpy of manganese very high ?

key_points: Mn2+ has half-filled 3d5 configuration which is highly stable
Removing the third electron disturbs this stable half-filled configuration

sub_questions.solution: Manganese (Mn) has the configuration [Ar] 3d5 4s2. After losing two electrons, Mn2+ has the configuration [Ar] 3d5, which is a half-filled d subshell. This half-filled configuration is exceptionally stable due to extra exchange energy. Removing the third electron would disturb this stable half-filled arrangement, requiring a very high amount of energy. Hence, the third ionization enthalpy of Mn is exceptionally large.

sub_questions.text: Zn, Cd और Hg को संक्रमण तत्व क्यों नहीं माना जाता है ?
sub_questions.text_english: Why Zn, Cd and Hg are not regarded as transition elements ?

key_points: Transition elements must have partially filled d orbitals in ground state or in common oxidation states
Zn, Cd and Hg have completely filled d orbitals (d10) in both ground state and common +2 oxidation state

sub_questions.solution: Transition elements are defined as elements that have partially filled d orbitals either in their ground state or in one of their stable oxidation states. Zn (3d10 4s2), Cd (4d10 5s2), and Hg (5d10 6s2) all have completely filled d orbitals in their ground state. Even in their most common oxidation state (+2), i.e., Zn2+ (3d10), Cd2+ (4d10), and Hg2+ (5d10), the d orbitals remain fully filled. Hence, they are not classified as transition elements.

Therefore, this complex exhibits geometrical isomerism.

sub_questions.text_english: The concentration of the reactant is reduced from 0.6 mol L–1 to 0.2 mol L–1 in 5 minutes in a first order reaction. Calculate rate constant of the reaction. (log 3 = 0.48)

key_points: Use first order rate equation: k = (2.303/t) × log([A]0/[A]t)

sub_questions.solution: For a first order reaction, k = (2.303/t) × log([A]0/[A]t). Here [A]0 = 0.6 mol L–1, [A]t = 0.2 mol L–1, t = 5 min. Therefore, k = (2.303/5) × log(0.6/0.2) = (2.303/5) × log 3 = (2.303/5) × 0.48 = 0.4606/5 = 0.2211 min–1. Hence, the rate constant k = 0.2211 min–1.

sub_questions.text_english: Rate constant k for the first order reaction is 2.54 × 10–3 s–1. Calculate the time required for three-fourth of the reactant to decompose. (log 4 = 0.60)

key_points: Three-fourth decomposed means [A]t = [A]0/4

sub_questions.solution: If three-fourths of the reactant decomposes, then the remaining amount is [A]t = [A]0 – (3/4)[A]0 = [A]0/4. Using the first order rate equation: t = (2.303/k) × log([A]0/[A]t) = (2.303/2.54×10–3) × log([A]0/[A]0/4) = (2.303/2.54×10–3) × log 4 = (2.303/2.54×10–3) × 0.60 = 1.3818/2.54×10–3 = 544.02 s ≈ 544 s.

questions.text: 8.0 g अवाष्पशील विलेय को 100 g डाइएथिल ईथर में घोलने पर बना विलयन 36.86 °C पर उबलता है जबकि शुद्ध डाइएथिल ईथर 35.60 °C पर उबलता है। विलेय का मोलर द्रव्यमान ज्ञात कीजिए। (डाइएथिल ईथर के लिए Kb = 2.02 K kg mol–1)
questions.text_english: A solution containing 8.0 g of a non-volatile solute in 100 g of diethyl ether boils at 36.86 °C whereas pure diethyl ether boils at 35.60 °C. Determine the molar mass of the solute. (Kb for diethyl ether = 2.02 K kg mol–1)

key_points: ΔTb = Kb × m, so m = ΔTb/Kb = 1.26/2.02 = 0.6238 mol/kg
Moles of solute = 0.6238 × 0.1 kg = 0.06238 mol

questions.solution: Elevation in boiling point: ΔTb = 36.86 – 35.60 = 1.26 K. Using the formula ΔTb = Kb × m, molality m = ΔTb/Kb = 1.26/2.02 = 0.6238 mol kg–1. Mass of solvent = 100 g = 0.1 kg. Moles of solute = molality × mass of solvent (in kg) = 0.6238 × 0.1 = 0.06238 mol. Molar mass of solute = mass/moles = 8.0/0.06238 = 128.2 g mol–1. Therefore, the molar mass of the solute is approximately 128 g mol–1.

298 K पर निम्नलिखित सेल का emf परिकलित कीजिए :
Sn | Sn2+ (0.001 M) || H+ (0.01 M) | H2(g) (1 bar) | Pt(s)
दिया है : E°Sn2+/Sn = –0.14 V, E°H+/H2 = 0.00 V [log 10 = 1]
questions.text_english:
Calculate emf of the following cell at 298 K :
Sn | Sn2+ (0.001 M) || H+ (0.01 M) | H2(g) (1 bar) | Pt(s)
Given : E°Sn2+/Sn = –0.14 V, E°H+/H2 = 0.00 V [log 10 = 1]

key_points: Cell reaction: Sn + 2H+ → Sn2+ + H2, n = 2

questions.solution: E°cell = E°cathode – E°anode = 0.00 – (–0.14) = 0.14 V. The cell reaction is: Sn(s) + 2H+(aq) → Sn2+(aq) + H2(g), with n = 2. The reaction quotient Q = [Sn2+]/([ H+]2 × P(H2)) = 0.001/((0.01)2 × 1) = 0.001/0.0001 = 10. Applying the Nernst equation at 298 K: Ecell = E°cell – (0.0591/n) × log Q = 0.14 – (0.0591/2) × log 10 = 0.14 – (0.02955 × 1) = 0.14 – 0.02955 = 0.1105 V ≈ 0.11 V.

Complete and balance the following equations :
(i) 4FeCr2O4 + 8Na2CO3 + 7O2 →
(ii) 5Fe2+ + MnO4– + 8H+ →

key_points: (i) 4FeCr2O4 + 8Na2CO3 + 7O2 → 8Na2CrO4 + 2Fe2O3 + 8CO2
(ii) 5Fe2+ + MnO4– + 8H+ → 5Fe3+ + Mn2+ + 4H2O

sub_questions.text_english: Explain why actinoid contraction is greater from element to element than lanthanoid contraction.

key_points: 5f orbitals have poorer shielding than 4f orbitals
Greater effective nuclear charge experienced per element in actinoids
Thus greater contraction per element in actinoids than in lanthanoids

sub_questions.solution: Actinoid contraction is greater from element to element than lanthanoid contraction because the 5f orbitals in actinoids are more diffuse and provide poorer shielding of nuclear charge compared to the 4f orbitals in lanthanoids. As a result, the effective nuclear charge experienced by the outer electrons increases more steeply across the actinoid series, leading to a larger decrease in atomic/ionic radius per element compared to the lanthanoid series.

sub_questions.text_english: [Fe(H2O)6]2+ is paramagnetic whereas [Fe(CO)5] is diamagnetic. Justify the statement. [Atomic number of Fe = 26]

key_points: Fe is 26: [Ar] 3d6 4s2; Fe2+ is [Ar] 3d6
H2O is a weak field ligand — no pairing occurs, 4 unpaired electrons in [Fe(H2O)6]2+ → paramagnetic
CO is a strong field ligand — forces pairing, 0 unpaired electrons in [Fe(CO)5] → diamagnetic

sub_questions.solution: Fe (Z=26) has configuration [Ar] 3d6 4s2. In [Fe(H2O)6]2+, iron is in +2 state (3d6). H2O is a weak field ligand, so it does not cause pairing of electrons. The 3d6 configuration in a weak field gives 4 unpaired electrons, making the complex paramagnetic. In [Fe(CO)5], iron is in zero oxidation state (3d6 4s2, i.e., d8 in zero-valent state). CO is a strong field ligand that causes complete pairing of d electrons. All electrons are paired, giving a diamagnetic complex with zero unpaired electrons.

sub_questions.text_english: On the basis of crystal field theory write the electronic configuration for d4 ion if Δ0 < P.

key_points: When Δ0 < P (weak field), electrons occupy eg before pairing in t2g
d4 in weak field: t2g3 eg1 (high spin), 4 unpaired electrons

sub_questions.solution: When Δ0 < P (crystal field splitting energy is less than the pairing energy), the ligand field is weak. In this case, electrons prefer to occupy higher energy eg orbitals rather than pair up in the lower t2g orbitals (Hund's rule is followed). For a d4 ion in weak field (Δ0 < P), the configuration is t2g3 eg1. This gives a high-spin complex with 4 unpaired electrons.

Major product is 1-(1-bromoethyl)-4-nitrobenzene

sub_questions.solution: When 1-ethyl-4-nitrobenzene (having a –CH2CH3 side chain and –NO2 group on the ring) is treated with Br2 in the presence of heat (or light), the reaction proceeds by a free radical mechanism. Bromination occurs at the benzylic carbon (the carbon directly attached to the benzene ring) of the ethyl group, giving the major product 1-(1-bromoethyl)-4-nitrobenzene: the –CH2CH3 group becomes –CHBrCH3.

sub_questions.text_english: Define Chirality.

key_points: A molecule is chiral if it is non-superimposable on its mirror image

sub_questions.solution: Chirality is the property of a molecule (or object) of being non-superimposable on its mirror image. A chiral molecule exists as two non-superimposable mirror images called enantiomers. A carbon atom bearing four different substituents is called a chiral (or asymmetric) centre and is the most common source of chirality in organic molecules.

sub_questions.text: SN1 अभिक्रिया में रेसिमीकरण क्यों होता है ?
sub_questions.text_english: Why racemisation occurs in SN1 reaction ?

key_points: SN1 proceeds through a planar carbocation intermediate
Nucleophile can attack from either side equally
Gives equal amounts of both enantiomers — racemic mixture

sub_questions.solution: In an SN1 reaction, the rate-determining step involves the formation of a planar (sp2) carbocation intermediate. Since the carbocation is flat, the incoming nucleophile can attack with equal probability from either face of the plane (front or back). This leads to the formation of equal amounts of both the R and S configuration products, resulting in a racemic mixture (racemisation).

sub_questions.text: रोज़ेनमुंड अपचयन
sub_questions.text_english: Rosenmund's reduction

key_points: Acid chloride reduced to aldehyde by H2 over Pd/BaSO4 catalyst

sub_questions.solution: Rosenmund's reduction: An acid chloride (RCOC l) is reduced to the corresponding aldehyde (RCHO) by passing hydrogen gas over a palladium catalyst supported on barium sulphate (Pd/BaSO4) in xylene solvent. The BaSO4 support poisons the catalyst slightly to prevent over-reduction to alcohol. Reaction: RCOCl + H2 → RCHO + HCl (Pd/BaSO4, xylene).

sub_questions.text: कैनिज़ारो अभिक्रिया
sub_questions.text_english: Cannizzaro's reaction

key_points: Aldehydes without α-hydrogen undergo disproportionation with conc. NaOH
One molecule is oxidised to carboxylate salt; another is reduced to alcohol

sub_questions.solution: Cannizzaro's reaction: Aldehydes that do not have any α-hydrogen atom undergo a disproportionation reaction on treatment with concentrated NaOH. One molecule of the aldehyde is oxidised to the corresponding carboxylate anion (RCOO–) while another molecule is simultaneously reduced to the corresponding alcohol (RCH2OH). Example: 2HCHO + NaOH(conc.) → HCOONa + CH3OH (formaldehyde gives formate salt and methanol).

sub_questions.text: हेल–फोलार्ड–जेलिन्स्की अभिक्रिया
sub_questions.text_english: Hell – Volhard – Zelinsky reaction

key_points: Carboxylic acids with α-H react with Cl2 or Br2 in presence of red phosphorus
α-halogenated carboxylic acid is obtained

sub_questions.solution: Hell–Volhard–Zelinsky (HVZ) reaction: Carboxylic acids containing an α-hydrogen are treated with chlorine or bromine in the presence of a small amount of red phosphorus (catalyst). Halogenation occurs selectively at the α-carbon to give an α-halo carboxylic acid. Example: CH3COOH + Br2 (red P) → CH2BrCOOH + HBr (bromoacetic acid is the product).

sub_questions.text_english: Define Denaturation as related to proteins.

key_points: Denaturation is the disruption of the secondary, tertiary, and quaternary structure of a protein without breaking peptide bonds
Caused by heat, pH change, or chemicals, leading to loss of biological activity

sub_questions.solution: Denaturation of a protein refers to a process in which the natural three-dimensional structure of a protein (secondary, tertiary, and quaternary) is disrupted without breaking the peptide bonds. It is caused by physical agents like heat and UV radiation, or chemical agents like acids, bases, and heavy metals. The protein loses its biological activity upon denaturation. Example: coagulation of egg white on boiling.

sub_questions.text: ओलिगोसैकैराइड को परिभाषित कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Define Oligosaccharides.

key_points: Carbohydrates formed by condensation of 2 to 10 monosaccharide units
Joined by glycosidic bonds; example: sucrose (disaccharide)

sub_questions.solution: Oligosaccharides are carbohydrates that are formed by the condensation of 2 to 10 monosaccharide units joined together by glycosidic bonds with the elimination of water molecules. They are classified as disaccharides (2 units), trisaccharides (3 units), and so on. Common examples include sucrose (glucose + fructose), maltose (glucose + glucose), and lactose (glucose + galactose).

sub_questions.text: संरचना के आधार पर ऐमिलोस तथा ऐमिलोपेक्टिन के मध्य अंतर कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: On the basis of structure differentiate between Amylose and Amylopectin.

key_points: Amylose: unbranched, helical chain of α-D-glucose units linked by α-1,4-glycosidic bonds (~15-20% of starch)
Amylopectin: branched chain with α-1,4-glycosidic bonds in the main chain and α-1,6-glycosidic bonds at branch points (~80-85% of starch)

sub_questions.solution: Amylose is the water-soluble, unbranched (linear) component of starch. It consists of glucose units joined by α-1,4-glycosidic bonds forming a long helical chain, and constitutes about 15–20% of starch. Amylopectin is the water-insoluble, branched component of starch (~80–85%). Its main chain has α-1,4-glycosidic linkages, while branching occurs via α-1,6-glycosidic bonds approximately every 24–30 glucose units.

sub_questions.text: यदि DNA के थायमीन युक्त न्यूक्लिओटाइड का जलअपघटन किया जाए तो कौन-कौन से उत्पाद बनेंगे ?
sub_questions.text_english: What products would be formed when a nucleotide from DNA containing thymine is hydrolysed ?

key_points: Thymine (nitrogenous base)
Deoxyribose sugar (2-deoxyribose)
Phosphoric acid

sub_questions.solution: When a nucleotide from DNA containing thymine is hydrolysed, three products are obtained: (1) Thymine — the nitrogenous base; (2) 2-Deoxyribose — the pentose sugar (deoxyribose sugar); and (3) Phosphoric acid (H3PO4) — the phosphate component. A nucleotide = nitrogenous base + pentose sugar + phosphate group, so hydrolysis breaks these components apart.

sub_questions.text: आप ग्लूकोस अणु में पाँच –OH समूहों की उपस्थिति कैसे स्पष्ट करेंगे जो भिन्न कार्बन परमाणुओं से जुड़े हैं ?
sub_questions.text_english: How will you explain the presence of five –OH groups in glucose molecule which are attached to different carbon atoms ?

key_points: Glucose reacts with five equivalents of acetic anhydride to give glucose pentaacetate
This confirms the presence of five free –OH groups on different carbons

sub_questions.solution: The presence of five –OH groups on different carbon atoms in glucose is confirmed by treating glucose with acetic anhydride. Glucose reacts with five molecules of acetic anhydride to form glucose pentaacetate (penta-O-acetylglucose). Since each –OH group reacts with one molecule of acetic anhydride (–OH + (CH3CO)2O → –OCOCH3 + CH3COOH), the formation of five acetyl derivatives confirms that there are five –OH groups each on a different carbon atom.

sub_questions.solution: Glucose contains an aldehyde group (–CHO) in its open chain form. It undergoes nucleophilic addition with HCN at the carbonyl carbon (C1). questions.text_english: Like NH3, nitrogen atom of amine is trivalent and carries an unshared pair of electrons. sub_questions.text_english: Why primary amines have higher boiling points than tertiary amines ?

key_points: Primary amines form extensive intermolecular hydrogen bonds (two N–H bonds available)
Tertiary amines have no N–H bond, so no hydrogen bonding, hence lower boiling points

sub_questions.solution: Primary amines have higher boiling points than tertiary amines because primary amines can form extensive intermolecular hydrogen bonds through their two N–H bonds. This requires more energy to break these associations during boiling. Tertiary amines have no hydrogen atom attached to nitrogen, so they cannot form hydrogen bonds with each other. As a result, tertiary amines have weaker intermolecular forces and lower boiling points than primary amines of comparable molecular mass.

questions.text_english: Osmosis is a process by which the molecules of a solvent pass from a solution of low solute concentration to a solution of high solute concentration through a semi-permeable membrane. Osmotic pressure is a colligative property. When the applied pressure on a solution exceeds its osmotic pressure, reverse osmosis occurs. When two solutions are separated by a semipermeable membrane and they have same osmotic pressure they are said to be isotonic. Of the two solutions separated by a semipermeable membrane, if one is a lower osmotic pressure, it is said to be hypotonic relative to the second solution. If it has a higher osmotic pressure, than the second solution, it is said to be hypertonic relative to the second solution. The osmotic pressure associated with the fluid inside the blood cell is equivalent to that of 0.9% (mass/volume) sodium chloride solution called normal saline solution and it is safe to inject intravenously. Osmotic pressure is vital in daily life and nature. It helps in explain, why IV fluids match blood's osmotic pressure, its also the principle behind food preservation using salt or sugar.

sub_questions.text: CaCl2 (i = 2.59) के उस द्रव्यमान का परिकलन कीजिए जिसे 2.46 L जल में घोलने पर परासरण दाब 27 °C पर 0.70 atm हो जाए। [दिया है : R = 0.082 L atm K–1 mol–1, CaCl2 का मोलर द्रव्यमान = 111 g mol–1]
sub_questions.text_english: Calculate the amount of CaCl2 (i = 2.59) dissolved in 2.46 litre of water such that its osmotic pressure is 0.70 atm at 27°C. [Given : R = 0.082 L atm K–1 mol–1, molar mass of CaCl2 = 111 g mol–1]

key_points: π = iMRT → M = π/(iRT)

sub_questions.solution: Using the modified osmotic pressure equation for electrolytes: π = iMRT, where π = 0.70 atm, i = 2.59, R = 0.082 L atm K–1 mol–1, T = 27 + 273 = 300 K. Molarity M = π/(iRT) = 0.70/(2.59 × 0.082 × 300) = 0.70/63.726 = 0.01098 mol L–1. Moles of CaCl2 = M × V = 0.01098 × 2.46 = 0.02701 mol. Mass of CaCl2 = moles × molar mass = 0.02701 × 111 = 2.998 g ≈ 3.0 g.

sub_questions.text_english: When raisins are kept in water, they get swollen. Name the phenomenon involved in this process.

key_points: Osmosis

sub_questions.solution: The phenomenon involved is Osmosis. Raisins are hypertonic (have a higher solute concentration) relative to the surrounding water. Water molecules flow from the hypotonic region (plain water) through the semi-permeable membrane of the raisin's skin into the hypertonic region (inside the raisin) by osmosis, causing the raisins to swell.

sub_questions.text: अन्य अणुसंख्य गुणधर्मों की अपेक्षा परासरण दाब क्यों अधिक लाभप्रद है ?
sub_questions.text_english: Why osmotic pressure is more advantageous than other colligative properties ?

key_points: Measured at room temperature (no heating required)
Very large numerical value even for dilute solutions — easier to measure accurately
Suitable for macromolecules like proteins and polymers

sub_questions.solution: Osmotic pressure is more advantageous than other colligative properties (like elevation of boiling point or depression of freezing point) because it can be measured at room temperature without heating or cooling the solution. Its magnitude is very large even for very dilute solutions, making it easier to measure accurately. It is particularly useful for determining molar masses of large molecules such as proteins and polymers where the changes in boiling or freezing point would be too small to measure.

sub_questions.text_english: Which phenomenon is responsible for desalination of sea water ?

key_points: Reverse osmosis

sub_questions.solution: Reverse osmosis is responsible for the desalination of sea water. When a pressure greater than the osmotic pressure of sea water is applied, water molecules are forced to pass from the salt water (high solute concentration) through a semi-permeable membrane to the pure water side (low concentration), which is the reverse of normal osmosis. This process removes dissolved salts and produces fresh drinking water from sea water.

'A' on treatment with iodine and sodium hydroxide gives 'C' and in presence of H2SO4 at 413 K gives 'D' (C4H10O). 'D' on reaction with excess of HI gives 'E'. sub_questions.text_english:
Write the reagents which are used in the given conversions :
(i) Phenol to 2, 4, 6 – tribromophenol
(ii) Propene to propan–1–ol
(iii) Butan–2–one to butan–2–ol

key_points: (i) Br2 water (aqueous bromine)
(ii) BH3/THF followed by H2O2/NaOH (hydroboration-oxidation) OR cold dilute H2SO4 (acid catalysed hydration, Markovnikov)
(iii) NaBH4 or LiAlH4 (or H2/Ni) — reduction of ketone

sub_questions.solution: Conversion (i): Phenol to 2,4,6-tribromophenol requires Br2/water (aqueous bromine solution). The –OH group in phenol activates the ring strongly, so three bromine atoms substitute at the 2, 4, and 6 positions simultaneously without any Lewis acid catalyst. Conversion (ii): Propene to propan-1-ol (anti-Markovnikov) requires BH3·THF followed by H2O2/NaOH (hydroboration-oxidation), which adds –OH to the less substituted carbon. Conversion (iii): Butan-2-one (a ketone) to butan-2-ol requires a reducing agent such as NaBH4 (sodium borohydride) or LiAlH4, or catalytic hydrogenation (H2/Ni), which reduces the ketone carbonyl to a secondary alcohol.

sub_questions.text_english: Explain the mechanism of acid catalyzed hydration of alkene to form corresponding alcohol.

key_points: Step 1: Protonation of alkene double bond by H+ to form carbocation (electrophilic addition)
Step 2: Attack of water molecule on carbocation to form oxonium ion
Step 3: Deprotonation of oxonium ion to give the alcohol

sub_questions.solution: The mechanism of acid catalysed hydration of alkene has three steps. Step 1 (Protonation): The π electrons of the alkene attack the proton (H+) from the acid catalyst (e.g., H2SO4 or H3PO4), following Markovnikov's rule. The proton adds to the carbon bearing more hydrogen atoms, giving the more stable carbocation at the carbon with fewer hydrogen atoms. Step 2 (Nucleophilic attack): A water molecule acts as a nucleophile and donates its lone pair of electrons to the carbocation, forming an oxonium ion (protonated alcohol). Step 3 (Deprotonation): The oxonium ion loses a proton to water (or base) to give the final alcohol product, regenerating the acid catalyst.

How will you convert the following :
(i) Propanone to Propene
(ii) Benzoic acid to Benzaldehyde
(iii) Benzene to m-Nitroacetophenone

key_points: (i) Propanone → reduce with Zn-Hg/HCl (Clemmensen) or NH2NH2/KOH (Wolff-Kishner) → propane, then not propene; OR propanone → with Grignard then dehydration to give propene via propan-2-ol
(ii) Benzoic acid → acid chloride (SOCl2) → Rosenmund reduction (H2/Pd-BaSO4) → Benzaldehyde
(iii) Benzene → Friedel-Crafts acylation (CH3COCl/AlCl3) → Acetophenone → Nitration (HNO3/H2SO4) → m-Nitroacetophenone

sub_questions.solution: Conversion (i) — Propanone to Propene: Treat propanone with Zn(Hg)/HCl (Clemmensen reduction) to get propane; alternatively, reduce propanone with NaBH4 to propan-2-ol, then dehydrate with conc. H2SO4 at 443 K to give propene. Conversion (ii) — Benzoic acid to Benzaldehyde: First convert benzoic acid to benzoyl chloride using SOCl2 (or PCl5). Then perform Rosenmund reduction by passing H2 gas over palladium on barium sulphate (Pd/BaSO4) catalyst in xylene at 100°C; this selectively reduces the acid chloride to benzaldehyde without further reduction. Conversion (iii) — Benzene to m-Nitroacetophenone: First perform Friedel-Crafts acylation of benzene using acetyl chloride (CH3COCl) and anhydrous AlCl3 to give acetophenone (methyl phenyl ketone). Since the –COCH3 group is a meta-director, nitration of acetophenone with a mixture of conc. HNO3 and conc. H2SO4 (mixed acid) gives m-nitroacetophenone.

sub_questions.solution: Nucleophilic addition of HCN to carbonyl compounds depends on the electrophilicity of the carbonyl carbon and steric accessibility. Electron-donating alkyl groups reduce electrophilicity, and bulky groups cause steric hindrance. Acetaldehyde (CH3CHO) is most reactive because it has only one small methyl group and one H — less steric hindrance and the carbon is more electrophilic. Acetone [(CH3)2C=O] is less reactive due to two methyl groups increasing electron density. Di-tert-butyl ketone [(CH3)3C]2C=O is least reactive due to extreme steric crowding and maximum electron donation. Increasing order of reactivity toward HCN: (CH3)3CC(=O)C(CH3)3 < (CH3)2C=O < CH3CHO.

sub_questions.text:
उन यौगिकों की पहचान कीजिए जो ऐल्डॉल संघनन देंगे :
HCHO, C6H5CHO, CH3CHO, cyclopentanone
sub_questions.text_english:
Identify the compounds, which would undergo Aldol condensation :
HCHO, C6H5CHO, CH3CHO, cyclopentanone

key_points: Aldol condensation requires at least one α-hydrogen
CH3CHO (acetaldehyde) and cyclopentanone have α-hydrogens → undergo Aldol
HCHO and C6H5CHO have no α-hydrogen → do not undergo Aldol

sub_questions.solution: Aldol condensation requires the presence of at least one α-hydrogen atom (a hydrogen on the carbon adjacent to the carbonyl group). HCHO (formaldehyde) has no carbon attached to the carbonyl carbon — no α-H, so it cannot undergo Aldol condensation. C6H5CHO (benzaldehyde) has no α-H (the carbonyl carbon is directly attached to the benzene ring) — cannot undergo Aldol. CH3CHO (acetaldehyde) has three α-hydrogen atoms on the methyl group — can undergo Aldol condensation. Cyclopentanone has α-hydrogen atoms on carbons adjacent to the C=O group — can undergo Aldol condensation. Therefore, CH3CHO and cyclopentanone will undergo Aldol condensation.

sub_questions.text:
निम्नलिखित यौगिक युगलों में विभेद करने के लिए सरल रासायनिक परीक्षण दीजिए :
(i) एसीटोफीनॉन एवं बेन्जोफीनोन
(ii) प्रोपैनैल एवं प्रोपेनोन
(iii) पेन्टेन–2–ऑन एवं पेन्टेन–3–ऑन
sub_questions.text_english:
Give chemical tests to distinguish between the following pairs of compounds :
(i) Acetophenone and Benzophenone
(ii) Propanal and Propanone
(iii) Pentan–2–one and Pentan–3–one

key_points: (i) Iodoform test: acetophenone (CH3CO–) gives yellow iodoform precipitate with I2/NaOH; benzophenone does not
(ii) Tollens' test or Fehling's test: propanal (aldehyde) gives silver mirror / brick-red precipitate; propanone (ketone) does not
(iii) Iodoform test: pentan-2-one (CH3CO–) gives iodoform; pentan-3-one does not

sub_questions.solution: Test (i) — Acetophenone vs. Benzophenone: Iodoform test. Add I2/NaOH to both compounds. Acetophenone has a –COCH3 group and gives a yellow precipitate of iodoform (CHI3) with a characteristic smell. Benzophenone has no methyl group next to the carbonyl and does not give iodoform. Test (ii) — Propanal vs. Propanone: Tollens' reagent test. Add Tollens' reagent (ammoniacal AgNO3) to both. Propanal is an aldehyde and reduces Tollens' reagent to give a shiny silver mirror on the walls of the test tube. Propanone (a ketone) does not reduce Tollens' reagent. Test (iii) — Pentan-2-one vs. Pentan-3-one: Iodoform test. Pentan-2-one (CH3COCH2CH2CH3) has a –COCH3 group and gives a yellow iodoform precipitate with I2/NaOH. Pentan-3-one (CH3CH2COCH2CH3) has no methyl group adjacent to carbonyl and does not give iodoform.

sub_questions.text: निम्नलिखित अम्लों में से कौन प्रबलतर है और क्यों ? CH2FCOOH, CH3COOH
sub_questions.text_english: Which of the following acids is stronger and why ? CH2FCOOH, CH3COOH

key_points: CH2FCOOH (fluoroacetic acid) is stronger
Fluorine is highly electronegative, exerts –I (inductive) effect, stabilises carboxylate anion

sub_questions.solution: CH2FCOOH (fluoroacetic acid) is stronger than CH3COOH (acetic acid). The fluorine atom in CH2FCOOH is highly electronegative and exerts a strong electron-withdrawing inductive effect (–I effect) through the C–F bond. This effect withdraws electron density from the carboxylate anion (CH2FCOO–), stabilising it and making the anion more stable. Greater stability of the conjugate base (carboxylate ion) means greater tendency to donate a proton, hence a stronger acid. CH3COOH has an electron-donating methyl group (+I effect) which destabilises the carboxylate anion, making it a weaker acid.

sub_questions.text:
निम्नलिखित यौगिकों को उनके क्वथनांकों के बढ़ते क्रम में व्यवस्थित कीजिए :
CH3OCH3, CH3CH2CH3, CH3CH2OH, CH3CHO
sub_questions.text_english:
Arrange the following compounds in the increasing order of their boiling points :
CH3OCH3, CH3CH2CH3, CH3CH2OH, CH3CHO

key_points: Propane (bp –42°C) < Dimethyl ether (bp –24°C) < Acetaldehyde (bp 20°C) < Ethanol (bp 78°C)
Alkanes lowest, then ethers, then aldehydes, then alcohols (H-bonding highest)

sub_questions.solution: Boiling points depend on the type and strength of intermolecular forces. CH3CH2CH3 (propane, bp –42°C) has only weak van der Waals forces. CH3OCH3 (dimethyl ether, bp –24°C) is polar but cannot form H-bonds with itself. CH3CHO (acetaldehyde, bp 20°C) is more polar than ether due to the C=O dipole and has stronger dipole–dipole interactions. CH3CH2OH (ethanol, bp 78°C) forms strong intermolecular hydrogen bonds (–OH…O) and has the highest boiling point. Increasing order: CH3CH2CH3 < CH3OCH3 < CH3CHO < CH3CH2OH.

sub_questions.text:
NaCl के 0.1 mol L–1 विलयन की चालकता 1.06 × 10–2 S cm–1 है। इसकी मोलर चालकता और वियोजन मात्रा परिकलित कीजिए।
λ°Na+ = 50.1 S cm2 mol–1, λ°Cl– = 76.5 S cm2 mol–1
sub_questions.text_english:
The conductivity of 0.1 mol L–1 solution of NaCl is 1.06 × 10–2 S cm–1. Calculate its molar conductivity and degree of dissociation.
λ°Na+ = 50.1 S cm2 mol–1, λ°Cl– = 76.5 S cm2 mol–1

key_points: Degree of dissociation α = Λm/Λ°m = 106/126.6 = 0.837 = 83.7%

sub_questions.solution: Molar conductivity Λm = κ × 1000/M (in S cm2 mol–1), where κ = 1.06 × 10–2 S cm–1 and M = 0.1 mol L–1. Therefore Λm = (1.06 × 10–2 × 1000)/0.1 = 106 S cm2 mol–1. Limiting molar conductivity Λ°m(NaCl) = λ°Na+ + λ°Cl– = 50.1 + 76.5 = 126.6 S cm2 mol–1. Degree of dissociation α = Λm/Λ°m = 106/126.6 = 0.8372 ≈ 0.837. Therefore, the molar conductivity is 106 S cm2 mol–1 and the degree of dissociation is approximately 0.837 or 83.7%.

sub_questions.text:
किसी गैल्वनी सेल में निम्नलिखित सेल अभिक्रिया होती है :
2Ag+(aq) + Zn(s) → 2Ag(s) + Zn2+(aq); E°(cell) = +1.56 V
विद्युत धारा के प्रवाह की दिशा की प्रागुक्ति कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english:
Following cell reaction occurs in a galvanic cell :
2Ag+(aq) + Zn(s) → 2Ag(s) + Zn2+(aq); E°(cell) = +1.56 V
Predict the direction of flow of current.

key_points: Zn is anode (oxidised), Ag+ is cathode (reduced)
Conventional current flows from cathode (silver electrode) to anode (zinc electrode) in the external circuit

sub_questions.solution: In this galvanic cell, zinc undergoes oxidation at the anode (Zn → Zn2+ + 2e–) and silver ions are reduced at the cathode (Ag+ + e– → Ag). Electrons flow through the external circuit from the anode (zinc electrode) to the cathode (silver electrode). Since conventional current is opposite to the direction of electron flow, conventional current flows from the cathode (silver electrode) to the anode (zinc electrode) in the external circuit.

sub_questions.text: प्राथमिक बैटरी और द्वितीयक बैटरी में अंतर कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Differentiate between a primary battery and a secondary battery.

key_points: Primary: non-rechargeable; reaction is irreversible; used once (e.g. dry cell, mercury cell)
Secondary: rechargeable; reaction is reversible; can be reused (e.g. lead storage battery, Ni-Cd cell)

sub_questions.solution: A primary battery cannot be recharged and is used only once. The electrochemical reactions are irreversible and cannot be easily reversed by applying an external electric current. Examples include dry cells (Leclanché cell) and mercury cells. A secondary battery (storage battery) can be recharged and used again. The electrochemical reactions are reversible, and the battery can be regenerated by passing an electric current through it in the reverse direction. Examples include the lead storage battery and the Ni-Cd battery.

sub_questions.text: 0.1 M KCl विलयन से भरे हुए एक चालकता सेल का प्रतिरोध 100 Ω है। यदि उसी सेल का प्रतिरोध 0.01 mol L–1 KCl विलयन भरने पर 300 Ω हो, तो 0.01 mol L–1 KCl विलयन की चालकता एवं मोलर चालकता परिकलित कीजिए। 0.1 M KCl विलयन की चालकता 1.29 × 10–2 S cm–1 है।
sub_questions.text_english: Resistance of a conductivity cell filled with 0.1 M KCl solution is 100 Ω. If the resistance of the same cell when filled with 0.01 mol L–1 KCl solution is 300 Ω, calculate the conductivity and molar conductivity of 0.01 mol L–1 KCl solution. The conductivity of 0.1 M KCl solution is 1.29 × 10–2 S cm–1.

key_points: Cell constant G* = κ × R = 1.29 × 10–2 × 100 = 1.29 cm–1

sub_questions.solution: First, find the cell constant. Cell constant G* = κ × R, where κ(0.1M KCl) = 1.29 × 10–2 S cm–1 and R(0.1M) = 100 Ω. G* = 1.29 × 10–2 × 100 = 1.29 cm–1. For the 0.01 mol L–1 KCl solution, R = 300 Ω. Conductivity κ(0.01M) = G*/R = 1.29/300 = 4.3 × 10–3 S cm–1. Molar conductivity Λm = (κ × 1000)/M = (4.3 × 10–3 × 1000)/0.01 = 4.3/0.01 = 430 S cm2 mol–1. Therefore, conductivity = 4.3 × 10–3 S cm–1 and molar conductivity = 430 S cm2 mol–1.

sub_questions.text: H2–O2 ईंधन सेल के कोई दो लाभ लिखिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Write any two advantages of H2 – O2 fuel cell.

key_points: High efficiency — converts chemical energy directly to electrical energy without combustion
Eco-friendly — the only by-product is water (no harmful emissions)

sub_questions.solution: Two advantages of H2–O2 fuel cells are: (1) High efficiency — they convert chemical energy directly into electrical energy without any combustion step, with efficiencies up to 70%, much higher than conventional heat engines limited by the Carnot cycle. (2) Eco-friendly — the only product formed is water (H2O), so there are no harmful emissions or pollutants, making it a clean energy source.

sub_questions.text: मक्र्यूरी सेल का सेल विभव अपनी संपूर्ण कार्य अवधि में स्थिर क्यों रहता है ?
sub_questions.text_english: Why does the cell potential of mercury cell remain constant throughout the life ?

key_points: Neither electrode reaction involves ions in solution
Anode: Zn(Hg) + 2OH– → ZnO + H2O + 2e–; Cathode: HgO + H2O + 2e– → Hg + 2OH–
No change in ion concentrations — Nernst equation gives constant potential

sub_questions.solution: The cell potential of a mercury cell remains constant throughout its working life because neither of the electrode reactions involves ions in aqueous solution. At the anode: Zn(Hg) + 2OH– → ZnO(s) + H2O + 2e–. At the cathode: HgO(s) + H2O + 2e– → Hg(l) + 2OH–. The overall reaction is: Zn(Hg) + HgO(s) → ZnO(s) + Hg(l). Since no ions are produced or consumed in solution, the concentrations of the species in the Nernst equation remain constant throughout the life of the cell, so the cell potential does not change.
